start.name: SEGAS (Union Fenosa Gas) Damietta LNG terminal, New Damietta, Damietta Governorate, Egypt
start.coord_basis: Coastal LNG/gas-grid node named in the sheet's StartState/Province='Damitta'. Used the SEGAS Damietta LNG plant as the citable Damietta-side grid anchor (town-level/plant-level, not necessarily the exact pipeline valve pad) -- Global Energy Observatory's 'Egypt (SEGAS) LNG Plant Egypt' listing gives lat 31.46872 lon 31.74732 for the plant at Damietta/Dumyat.

end.name: Egyptian LNG (ELNG) terminal, Idku (Edku), Beheira Governorate, Egypt
end.coord_basis: Matches sheet's EndPrefecture/District='Edku', EndState/Province='Beheira'. Used the Egyptian LNG (Idku) plant as the citable Idku-side grid anchor. Wikidata item 'Idku LNG' (Q17466774) gives 31 deg20'59.17"N, 30 deg19'1.88"E = 31.3498, 30.3172 -- converted and independently close (within ~0.2km) to a second commercial source (industryabout.com, 31.349163/30.320483) which could not be reached from this environment to re-verify live, so only the Wikidata URL is carried as evidence.

corridor_desc: Coastal Mediterranean trunk paralleling the coast/coastal road between New Damietta (Damietta Governorate) and Idku (Beheira Governorate), the delta's two LNG-export/grid-interconnection hubs. Straight-line distance between the two plant coordinates is ~136 km; the sheet's stated 165 km implies a route tortuosity of ~1.2x, consistent with a buried trunk following roads/canals along the coastal strip (through/near Baltim, Burullus, Rosetta-mouth area) rather than a straight offshore/beeline path.

facts.source: EGAS Annual Report 2018 (sheet seed ref); independent confirmation that a real 'Idku/Damietta' line exists in GASCO's operating network from GASCO/Petroleum Magazine Nov 2025 (p.55-57 area), which mentions camera monitoring installed at valve chamber (12) on 'khat Edko/Domiatt' (Idku/Damietta line) -- see route_refs.

notes: Searched EGAS Annual Report 2018 (pdftotext) and both Petroleum Magazine PDFs (Arabic, kashida-stripped) for an exact 'Damietta-Idku' grid-table row; none of the three documents list this specific named/lengthed line in their completed-projects tables (those tables cover only FY2017/18-2025/26 NEW construction, e.g. 'ElGamil/Domiatt 50km-42"', 'Edco/Abu-Hommus 29km-42"' -- different, newer lines). However, Petroleum Magazine Nov 2025 explicitly refers to an operational 'khat Edko/Domiatt' (Idku/Damietta line) in its camera-monitoring section, independently confirming this exact-named coastal trunk is real GASCO infrastructure, consistent with the brief's hypothesis. No public source gives the line's own precise endpoint stations, so I anchored both ends on the two cities' major, independently-coordinated LNG/gas-grid plants (SEGAS at Damietta, ELNG at Idku) at REDUCED accuracy (plant/city-level, not the literal pipeline tie-in point) -- distance math (165km stated vs ~136km straight-line) is plausible and supports the identification. Two independent sources agree closely on each endpoint coordinate (GEO + Wikidata/industryabout for Idku; GEO + Wikipedia narrative for Damietta/SEGAS). Recommend RouteAccuracy no better than 'low' given the plant-level (not pipeline-specific) anchoring.

start.name: Dahshur (Giza Governorate, markaz Badrashin) -- site of GASCO's Dahshur gas compressor station
start.coord_basis: The sheet's own StartLocation field already reads 'Dahshour' (not 'Damanhur') and the sheet's OtherLanguagePrimaryPipelineName is Arabic 'khat ghaz Dahshour-6 Oktobar' = 'Dahshur-6 October gas line' -- the pipeline's own name in Arabic says Dahshur, confirming the English 'Damanhur' in the PipelineName is a mistranscription. Coordinate is Dahshur town/archaeological-site center per Wikipedia (29 deg48'23"N 31 deg12'29"E); GASCO's real compressor station sits 'on the outskirts of the small town of Dahshour' per two independent trade sources (EgyptToday, Turboden/Siemens Energy press release), so this is a town-level anchor for a real, major, well-documented GASCO facility, not the individual compressor-station pad.

end.name: 6 October (6th of October City) power station / gas-distribution point, Giza Governorate, Egypt
end.coord_basis: Matches sheet's EndPrefecture/District='6 October'. EGAS's own 2018 Annual Report lists a completed '6 October power station gas supply pipeline (0.4 km-20")' and a separate '6 October power station' metering/reduction station -- i.e. EGAS's own grid vocabulary names '6 October power station' as the delivery point this class of line feeds. Coordinate is the '6 October CCGT Power Plant' listing (Global Energy Observatory), located at Al Jizah/Sheikh Zayed City area, Giza.

corridor_desc: Southwest of Cairo: from the Dahshur gas-grid compressor-station hub (west bank of the Nile, Giza Governorate, markaz Badrashin, near the Dahshur pyramid field) northwest across the desert-edge/agricultural fringe to 6th of October City / Sheikh Zayed City in western Giza. Straight-line distance between the two anchor points is ~32 km; the sheet's stated 65 km implies tortuosity of ~2x, plausible for a route threading around the Nile floodplain/canal network and desert-city road grid rather than a beeline.

facts.source: EGAS Annual Report 2018 (sheet seed ref) for the '6 October power station' grid vocabulary; sheet's own OtherLanguagePrimaryPipelineName for the Dahshur-vs-Damanhur naming resolution.

flags: name-misread:PipelineName says 'Damanhur' but StartLocation + the sheet's own Arabic OtherLanguagePrimaryPipelineName both say 'Dahshour' -- Damanhur (Beheira, near Alexandria) is ~170km straight-line from 6 October, which cannot fit a 65km pipeline; Dahshur (Giza, ~32km straight-line from 6 October) fits comfortably. Recommend correcting PipelineName from 'Damanhur-6 October' to 'Dahshur-6 October Gas Pipeline' -- flagged here per the research brief's instruction to reconcile, not applied to the sheet.
notes: This was the most decisively resolved of the four PIDs. Multiple independent lines of evidence converge on Dahshur (not Damanhur): (1) the sheet's own StartLocation field already says 'Dahshour'; (2) the sheet's own Arabic name field says 'Dahshour-6 October' plainly; (3) GASCO's Dahshur compressor station is independently, repeatedly documented (EgyptToday 2024, Turboden/Siemens Energy 2024, Petroleum Magazine Nov2025 and Dec2024 -- 'mahattat dawaghit Dahshour') as a major hub feeding 'janub al-wadi' (South Valley/Upper Egypt) and connected via GASCO's grid to Cairo-area consumers including 6th of October; (4) simple distance math rules out Damanhur (~170km, way over the stated 65km) and supports Dahshur (~32km straight-line vs 65km stated, a normal buried-pipeline tortuosity ratio). No source gives this specific named 'Dahshur-6 October' line's own two station coordinates, so both ends are anchored at town/plant level (Dahshur town center; 6 October CCGT power plant) rather than an exact valve pad -- recommend RouteAccuracy no better than 'low'.

start.name: Abu Madi onshore gas treatment plant / field, Nile Delta, Egypt -- exact site still not independently geocodable
start.coord_basis: Not resolved. Confirmed (youm7.com, elbalad.news, marefa.org, and GASCO's own Dec-2024 Petroleum Magazine, which names a joint 'Abu Madi and Talkha distribution-center' civil works project) that Abu Madi is a real, major, still-active GASCO/Petrobel gas treatment plant/distribution center -- Egypt's first gas discovery (1967), named for the shrine of Sidi Abu Madi. But sources actively DISAGREE on which governorate it is in: youm7/elbalad describe it as 'West Abu Madi area, Kafr El Sheikh Governorate' (near Baltim, ~180km north of Cairo, ~8km from the Mediterranean), while marefa.org's dedicated field article places it in 'markaz Belqas, Dakahlia Governorate' (delta interior, well south of the coast) -- these are materially different locations, not just imprecision. Checked OSM Overpass for name variants ('أبو ماضي'/'Abu Madi'/'Abou Madi') across a bounding box covering both Kafr El Sheikh coastal strip and northern Dakahlia (30.8-31.6N, 30.8-31.6E): zero industrial/plant/village features returned, only unrelated street names and a clothing shop. Nominatim searches for 'West Abu Madi', 'El Hamool', and Arabic variants returned nothing (then got rate/access-limited entirely from this environment). No named, checkable OSM node, Wikimapia id, or Wikipedia-coordinate exists for the plant itself.

end.name: Talkha (gas-fed power plant / GASCO distribution point), Talkha, Dakahlia Governorate, Egypt
end.coord_basis: Global Energy Observatory's 'Talkha CCGT Power Plant Egypt' listing gives lat 31.06225 lon 31.39211 for the gas-fed plant at Talkha City, Dakahlia -- ~3km from Talkha's Wikipedia town-center coordinate (31.05474, 31.37564), consistent with a specific industrial site on the town's outskirts rather than the town center itself. Carried forward unchanged from the prior research pass (2026-07-30), now independently re-confirmed via GEO.

corridor_desc: Unresolved START -- Talkha END well anchored, per the prior pass. New this pass: GASCO's own Dec-2024 Petroleum Magazine explicitly pairs 'Abu Madi and Talkha' as a single named distribution-center civil-development project, independently confirming these two sites are a real, linked GASCO operational axis (corroborating the pipeline's genuine existence/corridor), but it gives no coordinates. New governorate conflict (Kafr El Sheikh vs Dakahlia, see start.coord_basis) makes even a reduced-accuracy town-level start anchor unsafe without resolving which is correct -- did not adopt either.

facts.source: GEM sheet says 40km; Egypt Oil & Gas 'Guide to the Nile Delta's Oil and Gas Resources' (per prior pass) gives Abu Madi-Talkha I as 35km, 12in -- length discrepancy flagged by the prior pass, not re-litigated here (out of scope for this endpoints-only task).

flags: endpoint-mismatch:Abu Madi governorate is disputed across sources (Kafr El Sheikh per youm7/elbalad vs Dakahlia/markaz-Belqas per marefa.org) -- not merely imprecise, materially different regions; needs a tie-breaking primary source (EGPC/Petrobel facility map or a dated news item with a specific village name) before any coordinate can be adopted.
notes: Third pass on this PID (prior: 2026-07-28 initial, 2026-07-30 retry, both resolved:false). This pass did not close the gap but surfaced two new, useful facts: (1) GASCO's own Dec-2024 trade-magazine coverage explicitly pairs Abu Madi and Talkha as a joint distribution-center project, reinforcing that this is a real, still-maintained corridor (not a phantom/misfiled record); (2) an unresolved, previously-unnoticed GOVERNORATE-LEVEL conflict between sources on where Abu Madi actually is (Kafr El Sheikh coastal strip vs. Dakahlia/Belqas delta interior) -- these are ~80km+ apart, so this is a bigger and more specific problem than 'not geocodable', and is worth a dedicated primary-source check (EGPC/Petrobel field map) before this PID is revisited again. Per standing rule 2, no coordinate was fabricated or guessed to break the tie. Talkha end reconfirmed via GEO (new source, same coordinate as the prior pass's OGJ/Egypt-Oil-and-Gas-derived value).
